questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely to get back to your lane faster. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a traffic signal that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
You don't need to stop if the intersection looks clear.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat it like an all-way stop. Always come to a complete stop. Then look and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are hard to see and unpredictable. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Children on bikes may suddenly ride onto the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous than day driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead as you can during the day. Headlights from other cars can also create glare. Always use your headlights and drive with extra care at night.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, when should you slow down?

options.text: Before entering the curve.
After completing the curve.
In the middle of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. If you go too fast around a curve, your tires may lose grip on the road.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck body.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the body.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see cars directly behind the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?

options.text: Pull to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
Keep driving, but stay out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights, pull to the right side of the road and stop completely. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check traffic behind and beside you. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter before you change lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right, then to the left.

questions.question: What can speed up the process of alcohol leaving a person's system?

options.text: Nothing. Only time will allow all alcohol to leave a person's system.
Taking a cold shower.
Eating a large meal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing. Only time will allow all alcohol to leave a person's system.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind.
It distracts other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from the road. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk when using a cell phone.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, look for a gap large enough for you to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you drive better.
Make you feel better.
Weaken your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weaken your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not sleeping enough causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, lowers awareness, and weakens your judgment—just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn is allowed here.
A left turn is allowed only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn is allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line means the action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up so you don't cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Which of these driving skills is affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow reaction time, reduce coordination, lower alertness, and make it hard to focus.

questions.question: What can happen when you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: Nothing will likely happen.
You will be more alert.
You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and a stop arm, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Continue driving when you think the children are done exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out and lights flashing, stop completely. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled in and the lights turn off.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Just the driver
Only children
All occupants

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants
questions.explanation: Wyoming law requires all people in a moving vehicle to wear a safety belt, including the driver. The driver is responsible for making sure everyone follows this law. Children must use proper child-restraint systems.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They vibrate and make noise to warn drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They vibrate and make noise to warn drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn tired or distracted drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic signal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns that the road splits and you must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires do not grip as well. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance ramp should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the highway.
Force their way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Roadwork or maintenance is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roadwork or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction and maintenance work areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Traffic fines can be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To avoid tired driving dangers, take breaks every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Even without a crosswalk, you must yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and maintenance areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing or symbols.
